texts.arguments: Mr. Pothamshetti Manoj Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioner, would contend that the detaining authority has taken the crimes of 'law and order' into consideration and concluded that they are affecting the 'public order', which is illegal. The detaining authority relied on the aforesaid three (03) crimes for passing the detention order, but the allegations levelled against the detenu in the said crimes affect the specific individual and not the public at larger. i) He would further submit that the detention order was passed without application of mind and subjective satisfaction. Preventive detention of a person is an extreme measure resorted to by the State when ordinary criminal law is found not adequate to control his activities which cause disturbance to public order. On the other hand, learned Special Government Pleader appearing on behalf of the respondents would contend that the Detaining Authority having satisfied with the material available on record and considering the nature of offence and the manner in which it was committed by the detenu, passed the order of detention. He would further submit that the detenu was involved in the aforesaid crimes. The offences committed by the detenu are grave in nature. The Detaining Authority considering that there is every possibility of the detenu committing similar offences in future, which would again certainly affect the public order, issued detention order. There is no error in it. 15. As held by the Apex Court, personal liberty of the citizen which the law so sedulously and carefully protects can also be taken away by the procedure established by law, when it is used to jeopardize public good and not merely private interests. True distinction between 'public order' and 'law and order' was one of degree and extent of the reach of the act in question upon society. In one case, it might affect the problem of the breach of law and order and in another the breach of public order. The pendency of prosecution is no bar to an order of preventive detention and an order of preventive Smt.
